flags: minor: final paragraph ('division of labor... weather often determines when') nearly restates B; R013-02's stem and choice D also cue this answer
R013-01.notes: Author argues for stored resources + weather cue + predator/pollination benefits together. A extreme ('alone', 'little real effect'); C one factor only; D is the old view the author calls incomplete.

flags: minor: D is the longest choice (length cue)
minor: D paraphrases para 5 almost verbatim ('cue', 'not, by itself, the reason'), and overlaps with R013-01 B
R013-02.notes: Para 5 recasts weather as a regional signal to spend stored resources, explicitly not the reason for big crops. A contradicts 'weather may return'; B is the para-1 view; C unsupported.

flags: minor: A echoes the paragraph's next sentence ('more than the weather each tree happens to experience')
R013-03.notes: Distant synchronized masting under different local conditions shows coordination beyond local weather. B overstated (passage says weather does affect production); C 'full explanation' wrong; D off-topic.

R013-04.notes: Theory predicts strongest masting with specialists; least with generalists. A and D describe specialists; B describes food-limited (dependent) predators. Requires inverting via LEAST plus an inference step.

flags: minor: D 'predicted' is a good contextual trap since 'predicts' appears in the same sentence
R013-05.notes: 'Most pronounced' = most marked/conspicuous. A and C are the common 'speak/declare' senses; D tempting from nearby 'predicts'.

flags: minor: A lifts 'waste much of the effort' verbatim from the passage

minor: A's rationale ('little of the pollen in the air would reach its flowers') is a slight paraphrase stretch; the passage's mechanism is that the air would hold little pollen from neighbors, so few flowers fertilized. Still clearly best.
R013-06.notes: Para 4 last sentence states the out-of-step tree would waste much of its effort. B, C, D unsupported or contradicted.

flags: minor: A is an exact reversal of D, so test-wise students can narrow to the A/D pair
R013-07.notes: Paras 3-4 give benefits (predator satiation, pollination efficiency); para 5 opens 'Neither explanation tells us how trees... act together' and supplies the timing cue. A reversal trap; B and C unsupported.

R013-08.notes: 'No single tree designed' + 'over many generations' = shared, evolved, unplanned pattern. A contradicts 'no single tree designed'; B overreads 'come to depend on'; D the sentence concludes rather than introduces.

flags: minor: answer also restated in R013-01 D and R013-02 B, which reinforce it
R013-09.notes: Para 1: weather (warm/wet vs frost/drought) drove crop size. B, C, D are later or invented explanations.
